title: Six Ways to Fail at Creative Endeavors

entities.name: Doug Beyer
entities.description: The column's author on Wizards' creative team, who answers a reader question about planeswalkers and language.

entities.name: Jenna Helland
entities.description: Colleague of the author who wrote a recent Innistrad story.

entities.name: Carlo
entities.description: The reader who asks whether planeswalkers face a language barrier.

entities.name: Garruk
entities.description: A planeswalker used as an example in a question about a multilingual spark power.

entities.name: Jace
entities.description: A planeswalker and mind mage who could read minds to learn a language.

entities.name: Planeswalkers
entities.description: Beings with a spark able to travel between planes, whose lack of a language barrier is discussed.

entities.name: Innistrad
entities.description: A plane whose recent story was written by Jenna Helland.

events.summary: Doug answers Carlo's question: the creative team does not address planeswalkers' language barrier, since explaining it would cause more problems.
events.quote: we don't address it, as fun as it would be to go into the language problem once or twice, because over the long haul the cure would be worse than the disease.

events.summary: Doug considers a magical universal translator as a spark power but dislikes it.
events.quote: What if planeswalkers did have a magical universal translator?

relations.quote: my colleague Jenna Helland's recent Innistrad story
